why: The Rust side of the XCDR2 delimiter, returning the opaque `DHeaderScope`/`DHeaderMark` that the C FFI round-trips through an `int64`. RFC-0055's XCDR2 DELIMITED_CDR2 machinery. The RFC carries a CORRECTION dated 2026-07-26 that refutes its own premise: a default Jazzy peer serializes FINAL/XCDR1 on the wire, DDS-XTypes REJECTS an appendable writer against a FINAL reader, and #0267 turned out to be two Cyclone descriptor-builder bugs rather than a DHEADER gap. So the path is built, tested and PARKED -- `nros-c/src/cdr.rs`'s `const XCDR2: bool = false` makes every one of these a compile-time no-op today, waiting for a per-type `@appendable` signal that nothing yet emits. ROS 2's equivalent is not an API at all: extensibility is a property of the IDL annotation and the middleware acts on it, so there is no rclcpp/rclc verb to correlate with. See `c:cdr_begin_dheader`.
